newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Christopher wants concrete Israel-PLO results.
newsitem.headline: Christopher wants concrete Israel-PLO results.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher urged Israel and the PLO to achieve concrete results fast in negotiations resuming on Sunday after an outburst of violence that threatened their U.S.-brokered peace.

"The recent violence has demonstrated the great urgency of reaching some concrete results just as soon as possible," he told a joint news conference in Jerusalem with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Netanyahu said Israel sought a joint recommitment with the Palestinians to the peace accords but declined to set any target date for a long-delayed troop redeployment from the West Bank city of Hebron.
"What we seek is a simultaneous recommitment by both sides to the principles that both signed on to in Oslo," he said in a reference to their peace deals launched in 1993 in the Norwegian capital.
Asked about a date for the partial pullout from Hebron, Netanyahu, usually a master of the television sound bite, awkwardly sidestepped the question.

"I am not putting a date. I'm putting a conclusion. The satisfactory conclusion of the negotiation, I think from both sides, will be the date in which you'll be able to signify as a conclusion. And once it's concluded, I don't think there should be a delay in its implementation," he said in English.
Netanyahu sought to calm Palestinian fears that he wanted to rewrite the Oslo interim self-rule agreement signed by his Labour party predecessors.
"We did not propose opening the agreement. We suggested that within the confines of the existing agreement adjustments be made," he told the news conference.
Netanyahu wants to modify security arrangements for Jewish settlers in Hebron, the last of seven West Bank cities under the peace deals due to be given Palestinian self-rule.

"The prime minister assured me that he understands the context of these negotiations is to go forward with the implementation of the interim agreement which he understands there is an obligation to carry out," Christopher said.
"I don't have any doubt that the prime minister understands the urgency of these negotiations," he said.

Christopher was later due to meet Palestinian President Yasser Arafat before the scheduled start of talks between teams of lower-level Israeli and PLO negotiators at the Israeli border with the self-ruled Gaza Strip.
The talks at the Erez crossing were the outcome of last week's emergency White House summit spurred by clashes and gunbattles that claimed the lives of 58 Palestinians and 15 Israelis.

The Gaza talks, with the participation of Christopher's Middle East envoy Dennis Ross, centre on the partial Israeli pullback from Hebron delayed since March by Islamic suicide bombings in Israel and by Israeli security concerns.

It remained to be seen how the two sides would reconcile differences over Hebron and other issues, such as demands by Israel for tougher security arrangements and by Palestinians for easing of restrictions.
